beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley lays three cards face down. "Let's see the whole shape of this, not just today's."

beats.prompt: The past: the pause you sat in after the tour, before any of this deal news.
The present: the blend you'd only just started to find.
The future: what just came down on all of it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, quiz me. If the collapse was inevitable, why bother building carefully at all?"

options.text: Careful building isn't wasted — it's what let you actually see what was stagnant.
It means careful building is pointless, so stop trying.
Building has nothing to do with what collapsed.

elaboration: What falls apart was already unstable; the collapse just makes it visible — building the thing carefully was still how you found that out.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Everyone keeps telling me to rebuild exactly what I had. Is that the move?"

options.text: Not necessarily — sometimes the disruption is the only way to break the stagnation underneath.
Stagnation isn't something this card is about.

elaboration: Sometimes disruption is the only way to break stagnation — and resisting the change usually costs more than flowing with it.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the pause that steadied you, the blend you were only starting to trust, and the collapse that's clearing space for something less rigid."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think I've been mourning the wrong thing — it wasn't really working, not all the way. I can see that now that it's actually gone. I'm not scared to build the next version smaller and truer instead."
